ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE Law), as amended; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended; CSSF Regulation and CSSF Circular 21/782 on AML/CFT obligations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority of the UBO's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State prosecutor's office or national criminal records authority in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank or utility company; if notarized, certified copy is sufficient

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Sworn declaration executed before the Luxembourg notary

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every UBO, director, authorized signatory and high-level manager against the consolidated EU financial sanctions list (EU Council Regulation 269/2014), UN Security Council sanctions as implemented through Luxembourg Ministry of Finance, Luxembourg ACD (Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA) watchlists, OFAC SDN list for USD Swift Wire payment rails, and domestic CSSF PEP guidance. Where a PEP is identified, enhanced due diligence including source-of-wealth review and senior management approval is required. Screening results must be documented in the AML/KYC file and refreshed at least annually.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) portal, available at https://www.lbr.lu and via the guichet.lu administrative portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be in Latin alphabet and must not be contrary to Luxembourg public order. Non-Latin script names require a Latin transliteration. The legal form suffix 'Société à responsabilité limitée' or 'SARL' must be included. The statutory instrument may be drafted in French, German or Luxembourgish; the commercial trade name may be in English or another EU language, subject to RCS verification of availability.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name rejection is notified in writing by the RCS Clerk. Within 15 days, the applicant may submit a written request for reconsideration through the LBR online filing interface. If the rejection is confirmed, the applicant may appeal to the Luxembourg Administrative Tribunal within 3 months of notification. No extension of the 30-day reservation is available; a fresh reservation application must be filed once the initial window lapses.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office/service-provider address is permissible as the registered office if it is a real street address in Luxembourg where legal documents can be served, but the SARL must retain actual substance such as management functions, business records, a Luxembourg bank account and, for a freight forwarding business, personnel arranging dispatch and customs documentation. The Luxembourg tax authority and ACD may re-characterize the seat if no underlying economic activity is proven.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate; approximately 30–40% within the first 24 months of operation owing to AML/CFT controls, occasional CSSF on-site inspections, and VAT/ACD desk audits. Unannounced visits are rare for a clean low-risk ISIC 5229 business but may occur if sanctions screening flags any counterparty or if inconsistent substance indicators are identified.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Amended Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Articles 710-1 to 710-23 for the Société à Responsabilité Limitée), as reformed by the Law of 23 July 2016; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies and Annual Accounts
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés – RCS), operated under the Ministry of Justice
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association (Acte constitutif et Statuts) filed electronically via the LBR e-filing portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum subscribed share capital is €12,000 (12,000 shares of €1.00 par value). At least 25% of the cash subscription (€3,000) must be effectively paid up before the notary at incorporation; in-kind contributions must be fully paid up and supported by a statutory auditor's report within one year. The funds are blocked on a notary escrow account or in a blocked bank account in the name of the company in formation and released upon RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, by the sole shareholder, that: (1) the Company's subscribed share capital amounts to €12,000, divided into 12,000 registered shares of €1.00 each, fully subscribed and paid up to the minimum required by law (25% of the cash portion, i.e. €3,000); (2) the registered office is established at [address], Luxembourg, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg; (3) Mr/Ms [Name], born on [date], is appointed sole Manager (Gérant) of the Company, vested with full powers of administration and representation, signature being valid alone; (4) the Manager is authorized to complete registration before the Luxembourg Business Registers and the RESA, to obtain the establishment authorization, VAT, social security and all ancillary permits, and to open bank accounts in the Company's name; effective as of this date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Drafting and Capital Escrow Arrangement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg) and a Luxembourg credit institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Luxembourg notary to draft the articles of association compliant with Articles 710-1 to 710-23 of the Law of 10 August 1915. Determine the ISIC 5229 freight-forwarding objects clause and the registered office address with the landlord's written consent. Open a blocked capital account in the name of the SARL in formation at a Luxembourg bank or deposit the capital with the notary; verify payment of at least €3,000 (25% of €12,000) prior to signature. Complete AML/KYC and beneficial-ownership onboarding of each founder.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association
Passport or national ID of each founder and appointed manager
AML/KYC questionnaire and source-of-funds declaration
Written consent of landlord for registered office
Bank certificate of capital blocking (attestation de blocage) or notary account receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or notary rejects the dossier for KYC deficiencies, submit corrected ownership and source-of-funds evidence; if the objects clause is legally insufficient, revise the draft articles by notarial amendment before signature.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Incorporation Deed and Verification of Paid-up Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold a formal signing session before the notary. Each founder declares subscription to the issued shares; the notary verifies the effective payment of the minimum €3,000 cash portion and the availability of in-kind contribution valuations where applicable. The articles are authenticated and the first Manager (Gérant) is appointed with defined powers. Certified notarial copies are issued for subsequent filings.
required_dossiers: Finalized articles of association
Capital blocking certificate or notary account proof
Identity documents of all founders and the appointed manager
Initial beneficial-owner data for the RBE register
Auditor's report on in-kind contributions, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a defect (e.g., underpaid capital, ultra vires clause), the deed is deferred and corrected before re-notarization; unpaid capital must be topped-up on the escrow account and re-certified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) via the LBR e-filing portal / eJustice.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of notarisation, file the deed of incorporation and the articles through the RCS electronic system. Pay the lodgement fee (€23.87). Complete the RCS enterprise form containing legal name, registered office, objects, manager(s) and the €12,000 subscribed capital. Upon validation, the RCS assigns the registration number and issues the certificate of registration evidencing legal personality.
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation
Certified copy of the articles of association
Completed RCS electronic filing form
Proof of payment of the statutary filing fee
Manager's identity document and address confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query (observation), the notary submits a rectification file within 15 days; if registration is refused, an appeal may be lodged with the competent civil court within 30 days of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of Incorporation in the Official Electronic Companies Gazette (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The RCS automatically transmits the validated registration data to the RESA for statutory publication. Verify the RESA extract and confirm the publication is dated. Retain the published notice in the corporate minute book. The publication triggers the opposability period after which the incorporation can no longer be challenged on formal grounds.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate
RESA publication extract (generated by the gazette)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed or contains erroneous data, counsel files a rectification request with the RCS; monitor the 3-month opposition window after publication and respond to any third-party challenge by producing the notarized deed and RCS certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment Authorization (Autorisation d'établissement) and Ancillary Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy – General Directorate for Industry and Commercial Activities; ancillary: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) and Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the establishment authorization application on MyGuichet.lu for the regulated freight-forwarding activity (commissionnaire de transport / activités de transit) under the amended Law of 28 December 2023. Demonstrate the manager's professional competence and good repute. Upon issuance of the authorization, register for VAT (TVA) with the AEDT and enroll as an employer with the CCSS when hiring staff.
required_dossiers: Establishment authorization application form (MyGuichet.lu)
Criminal record certificate (certificat de bonne conduite, bul 3) of the manager
Professional qualification diploma or five years' relevant professional experience certificate
RCS extract
Occupancy consent and safety certificate for the registered office
VAT registration form for companies
CCSS employer registration file
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry refuses or conditions the authorization, the applicant may exercise the right to be heard within 15 days, cure the dossier, and appeal to the Administrative Tribunal within 3 months; interim suspension may be sought before the administrative court in case of imminent harm.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – General Directorate for Industry and Commercial Activities (Ministère de l'Économie – Direction de l'industrie et des activités commerciales)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Establishment Authorization) for freight forwarding and transit activities under the amended Law of 28 December 2023 concerning the authorization of certain commercial activities

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Administration)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Office-Based Administrative Activity: not a classified establishment (établissement classé) under the amended Law of 1 August 2018; no full EIA report or environmental operating permit required unless warehousing, truck-parking or handling operations are subsequently added
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Only municipal wastewater discharge parameters apply (pH 6–10, no toxic organic loads; connection to the communal sewer under the general regulation on wastewater); zero industrial VOC or combustion-source emission allowances; waste handling per the amended Law of 21 March 2017 with mandatory sorting and disposal through authorized waste-management channels

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the Grand-Ducal Fire and Rescue Corps (CGDIS) and the commune for the office premises; structural load inspection and workplace clearance by the Labour and Mines Inspectorate (ITM) under the Labour Code; occupational-file registration and appointment of a safety delegate once headcount exceeds statutory thresholds

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) — Luxembourg Inland Revenue, responsible for corporate income tax, net wealth tax and municipal business tax; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), responsible for VAT registration, VAT returns and all indirect tax audits; Administration des douanes et accises (ADA) for customs and export-clearance supervision. All statutory filings and registrations are channelled through the official MyGuichet.lu e-government portal and the eTVA electronic filing channel.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Luxembourg-resident SARL obtains its statutory tax identity through a two-step process: (1) incorporation before a notary and registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR/RCS), which automatically allocates the national business identification number (numerus matricule / NIF) and communicates it ex officio to the ACD and AEDT; (2) VAT registration by filing the standard VAT registration declaration (form 102 / MIF) with the AEDT via MyGuichet.lu, after which the entity receives a LU-prefixed 8-digit Luxembourg VAT identification number. A foreign undertaking without a corporate seat that performs taxable rail-freight activities in Luxembourg must register directly if it is established in the EU or EEA; a non-EU undertaking must appoint an AEDT-approved VAT fiscal representative having joint and several liability for Luxembourg VAT, and must file the home-country VAT certificate, constitutional documents and LBR extract. Freight forwarding under ISIC 5229 does not require a sectoral licence, so no additional authorisation is prerequisite for tax registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: the SARL is a fully opaque Luxembourg-resident corporation taxed at entity level on its worldwide income. The applicable tax burden comprises corporate income tax (CIT) at 15% on taxable income up to EUR 175,000 and 17% above that threshold, a 7% solidarity surcharge on the CIT, municipal business tax at the communal rate (6.75% in Luxembourg City), and net wealth tax at 0.5% on taxable net assets above the EUR 500,000 exemption, producing an aggregate top effective rate of 24.94% for the Luxembourg City SARL. No pass-through or check-the-box treatment is available under Luxembourg law; the SARL is within the territorial scope of full residence-based taxation, while foreign PE profits may be relieved under tax treaties and the Luxembourg participation exemption where applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not provide check-the-box elections for a SARL. The available statutory election and classification mechanisms relevant to a rail-freight SARL comprise: (i) tax unity (integration fiscale) allowing a resident parent company to elect consolidation with 75%+ subsidiaries; (ii) VAT grouping (assujetti unique) available since 1 January 2020 for affiliated entities with fixed establishments in Luxembourg; (iii) the substantial-participation capital-gains exemption election requiring a 12-month holding period and at least 10% shareholding or EUR 6 million acquisition cost; (iv) the participation exemption election for dividend income, applicable where the SARL holds at least 10% or a EUR 1.2 million participation; (v) ATAD anti-hybrid conformity elections, which are limited to eliminating hybrid mismatches and cannot confer pass-through character on a resident SARL; and (vi) fiscal-neutral reorganisation elections under the 2009 merger and reorganisation law for restructuring intermodal container-pool assets without exit taxation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) in conjunction with the European Central Bank (ECB) for euro monetary policy and payment system integrity; prudential conduct of banking and payment institutions is supervised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Total convertibility is guaranteed. Luxembourg is a euro-area founder member and imposes no exchange control regulation. Both current-account (services, freight, operational expenses) and capital-account (share capital, loans, dividends) movements are fully liberalised under Articles 63-66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, subject only to (i) EU financial sanctions and asset-freeze measures, (ii) anti-money-laundering controls under the Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02, and (iii) balance-of-payments statistical declarations to the BCL. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is unrestricted at the treasury level; the sole fiscal obstacle is the domestic 15% withholding tax on dividend distributions, reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for qualifying EU parents or under the relevant double taxation treaty.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No surrender obligation exists. Luxembourg has no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio and no central-bank repatriation requirement for export or service receipts. Freight-forwarding proceeds may be received and held in EUR, USD, CNY or any convertible currency and retained indefinitely in multicurrency accounts. Only generic BCL balance-of-payments threshold reporting applies to cross-border flows, and all transactions remain subject to the EU sanctions and anti-money-laundering framework.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque Internationale à Luxembourg, société anonyme (BIL)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (séquestre) and Operational Multicurrency Treasury Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE) - Spuerkeess
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
Operational EUR/CNY/USD Account; Trade Finance and Letter of Credit Desk
Operational Treasury Account and Trade Finance Facilities

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM as an ancillary collections channel; LOW as a treasury, escrow or trade-finance keeper. Legal constraints: Under Directive (EU) 2015/2366 (PSD2), an electronic money institution servicing a Luxembourg-established corporate must hold a CSSF licence or a valid EU passport; an offshore EMI without passporting may not lawfully hold operational funds. EMIs can neither accept deposits nor issue letters of credit or guarantees, and customer funds must be safeguarded, not banked. Recommended usage is limited to small ticket cross-border collections from shippers; the primary clearing, LC and FX lines must remain at a fully licensed Luxembourg credit institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The prevailing CSSF-supervised standard for a newly incorporated SARL is physical identification of at least one statutory manager and all UBOs at the bank counter or via a Luxembourg notary or consulate attestation. Remote onboarding is possible but conditional: (i) original or apostilled identity documents couriered to the bank, (ii) a mandatory recorded live video interview with compliance, (iii) certified English, French or German translations, and (iv) for the first board mandate, an original notarised board resolution. The bank will require the RCS certificate (extrait du registre de commerce) dated no earlier than three months, certified articles of association, proof of registered office and substance, and confirmation of ultimate beneficial ownership for the RBE register.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Eurasian rail transit crossing sanctioned jurisdictions (Russia, Belarus, transit points) triggering EU restrictive measures exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions compliance manual; route screening report showing no transit through embargoed borders or recourse to non-sanctioned corridors; contractual prohibition of sanctioned cargo and origin; counterparty sanction-screening declarations; pro-forma invoices and consignment notes (CIM/SMGS) evidencing each shipment; external legal opinion on sanctions architecture.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO chain with non-EU holdings, opaque trusts or nominee structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full chain-of-title organigram decoded to natural persons holding more than 25 per cent; notarised statutory declarations of beneficial ownership; certified passports and tax residence certificates of all UBOs; source-of-funds evidence (audited financial statements, bank references, asset custody statements); RBE registration receipt under the Law of 13 January 2019.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity, multi-jurisdiction freight-forwarding receipts with thin margins and high intermediate counterparty count.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master service agreements and framework contracts with cargo owners and rail operators; twelve-month treasury forecast and netting model; set of invoices, SAD customs declarations, waybills and rail consignment notes proving the intermodal loop; pre-approved list of all payment counterparties; confirmation of no crypto or instant-settlement rails; accounting system showing an audit trail for every inward flight.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection or shareholder loans at or near the EUR 12,000 statutory minimum giving rise to negative-equity working capital red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarial deed of incorporation with full subscription; bank credit advice evidencing payment of minimum legal capital; shareholder loan agreements with commercial interest, maturity and subordination clauses; projected cash-flow from confirmed freight bookings; evidence of substance including lease, payroll, director CVs and minutes of the management board.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inward shareholder funds are transmitted by SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA Credit Transfer for euro-area shareholders) referencing 'Apport en capital - [company name]' or 'Share capital contribution' to the SARL IBAN; for non-EU inbound flows, the sending bank must quote the ECB statistical purpose code where possible; the Luxembourg beneficiary bank will verify the notarised deed of incorporation and RCS registration before releasing funds and will file the transaction in the BCL balance-of-payments statistical return. Capital amounts must match the notarial subscription statement; injections of EUR 10,000 or above will in practice trigger standard source-of-funds documentation (copy deed, shareholder bank statement, board resolution approving the contribution).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Freight and logistics disbursements are settled over four rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for non-euro wire transfers to rail operators, terminal handlers and Chinese or Eurasian counterparties; (ii) SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant routed via TARGET2 for euro payments; (iii) commercial letters of credit under UCP 600 for substantial pre-payments, intermodal equipment procurement and rolling-stock deposits; (iv) MT202 COV for interbank reimbursement against the underlying trade. Documentary collection under URC 522 may be used for smaller port disbursements. Currency of settlement (EUR, USD, CNY) is confirmed against each transport contract and supported by the bank-approved FX conversion line.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD forward contracts (plain vanilla OTC)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) on CNY/offshore CNH where physical delivery is not available
FX swaps (spot against forward) for near-term liquidity management
Cross-currency swaps (XCCY) on EUR/USD and EUR/CNY term exposures
Zero-cost EUR/USD collar structures for freight tariff risk protection
European plain vanilla FX options on EUR/USD and EUR/CNY subject to an internal derivatives policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) and approval of statutory annual accounts (comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate act - not filed with a regulatory agency; AGM minutes retained in the statutory minute book at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of financial year-end; extension only by District Court order on just cause. Calendar-year SARL: AGM no later than 30 June.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene or approve accounts blocks all downstream filings; managers face civil liability toward the company and third parties; persistent default may be invoked in judicial dissolution and criminal fine proceedings against managers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual accounts (comptes annuels) with the Luxembourg Business Registers - RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after AGM approval and, in all cases, no later than 7 months after financial year-end. Calendar-year SARL: filing by 31 July; electronic filing via LBR e-file is mandatory.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine of EUR 500 to EUR 10,000 against managers; coercive astreinte up to EUR 1,250 per day of delay imposed by the court; joint and several civil liability; after sustained non-filing, RCS may initiate a strike-off (radication) procedure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of statutory registration data (Art. 8, Law of 19 December 2002)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days following the AGM that approves the annual accounts; if no AGM is held, within 15 days after expiry of the statutory 7-month approval window.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EUR 5,000; continued non-confirmation leads to formal warning and possible deregistration proceedings by LBR.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership data in the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once each calendar year, within 1 month after the AGM approving the annual accounts; additional confirmation due within 1 month of any change in beneficial ownership.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EUR 1,250 per natural person and EUR 2,500 per legal person for each breach; criminal penalties under the amended Law of 12 November 2004 for wilful false or withheld information, including imprisonment up to 5 years.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (déclaration d'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) - electronic Form via eCDF
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) - Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 May following the calendar tax year (standard); extension up to 31 December available for active electronic filers upon reasoned request lodged before 30 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fine up to EUR 5,000; taxation d'office under Art. 222 LIR with reversal of the burden of proof; late-payment interest at the statutory monthly rate (currently 0.6%) plus automatic 10% surcharge on unpaid assessed tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual net wealth tax return (impôt sur la fortune) and minimum net wealth tax settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Net wealth tax return filed jointly with the corporate income tax return due 31 May (standard); minimum net wealth tax of EUR 5,000 for a standard SARL payable through four quarterly advance instalments on the ACD instalment schedule.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late-payment surcharge; statutory default interest on arrears; execution proceedings (saisie/garnissement) after final assessment; persistent default triggers ACD enforcement against registered assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Chamber of Commerce contribution (contribution à la Chambre de Commerce)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Chambre de Commerce du Luxembourg - Centre Commun des Droits de Chambre
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually following the reference fiscal year, per the Chamber's contribution assessment notice; typical due date 30 April of the year following the reference year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Assessment enforced by the tax collector (Recette des contributions) as a liability attached to the registered commercial status; unpaid amounts bear statutory interest; persistent default triggers recovery proceedings and suspension of chamber voting rights.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent statutory audit (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) where the SARL exceeds at least two of the three thresholds at financial year-end: (i) balance sheet total above EUR 6,000,000; (ii) net turnover above EUR 12,000,000; (iii) average workforce above 50 employees. Mandatory regardless of size for companies required by their articles, by shareholders holding 10% or more, or for financial, insurance and securitisation undertakings. ISIC 5229 rail-freight forwarding SARL is a standard non-regulated commercial undertaking and remains audit-exempt while below the thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP pursuant to the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on annual accounts of undertakings (implementing EU Directive 2013/34/EU); IFRS as adopted by the EU mandatory for consolidated accounts of LU-listed parent undertakings and optional for voluntary consolidation; individual SARL statutory accounts must be prepared under Lux GAAP unless a permitted IFRS election applies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the amended Law of 13 January 2019, the SARL must file initial beneficial ownership details within 30 days of incorporation, update the RBE within 1 month of any change in ownership or control, and confirm at least once per calendar year, within 1 month following the AGM approving the annual accounts, that the registered UBO data remain accurate. Following the CJEU judgment of 22 November 2022 (C-37/20), public access to the RBE is restricted to parties demonstrating a legitimate interest, but the annual confirmation and update obligations remain fully in force.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (registre des parts sociales)
Register of Directors and Managers (registre des gérants)
Annual accounts and supporting accounting records (comptabilité)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,700 - USD 4,500 per annum (typical Luxembourg domiciliation, registered office, statutory representation and annual corporate secretarial package; mid-market USD 2,400 - USD 3,000 for a standard SARL)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 where audit-exempt (below EUR 6.0M balance sheet, EUR 12.0M turnover and 50 FTE thresholds); USD 6,000 - USD 28,000 per annum if a statutory audit becomes mandatory, depending on group structure and Lux GAAP engagement scope

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate in Luxembourg City for taxable profits above EUR 175,000; 15% CIT on the first EUR 175,000, 17% CIT above that amount, plus 7% solidarity surcharge and municipal business tax at the applicable communal rate.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP regime: 80% exemption for qualifying net IP income and gains, producing an effective aggregate rate of approximately 4.99%. R&D and investment tax credits are available. No general statutory tax holiday.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 102 (annual corporate income tax return for collective entities) filed electronically through MyGuichet.lu / eCIT Portal of the Administration des contributions directes.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly advance CIT instalments are due 10 March, 10 June, 10 September and 10 December.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a financial year ending 31 December, the e-filed return must be submitted by 31 December of the following calendar year; extensions are generally not automatic and require tax-agent representation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, RCS registration number, tax file number, registered office, ISIC/NACE activity code, SARL legal form and accounting period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies with a Luxembourg PE: enter the PE registration details in Luxembourg, foreign tax residence certificate, and local PE tax file number; appoint a Luxembourg tax representative.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial profit or loss per Luxembourg GAAP financial statements before tax adjustments, covering rail freight forwarding revenue, intermodal container transport income, subcontractor costs, lease charges and operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only include profit or loss attributable to the Luxembourg permanent establishment; attach PE-level financial statements and ensure cross-border intercompany charges are supported by transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box C - Taxable Income and Adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after adding back non-deductible expenses, hidden distributions and disallowed provisions, and after deducting loss carry-forwards, IP-box exempt income, participation exemptions and other statutory reliefs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute the Luxembourg taxable base under domestic tax law; claim treaty and EU Directive relief only where beneficial ownership and economic substance conditions are satisfied and evidenced.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing may trigger default assessment, administrative fines, and monthly late-payment interest of 0.6% on unpaid tax; intentional false filing exposes the taxpayer and responsible directors to criminal tax penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory Luxembourg withholding tax on dividends; 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for qualifying corporate shareholders holding at least 10% for 12 months; reduced DTA rates commonly 5%, 10% or 15% depending on the treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Relief at source is obtained by submitting to the Luxembourg paying agent a valid tax residence certificate from the shareholder's jurisdiction, beneficial-ownership declaration and supporting ownership/entitlement evidence before payment. Where tax has already been withheld, a refund claim must be filed with the Administration des contributions directes within the applicable statutory deadline, attaching the TRC and full ownership documentation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic Luxembourg rate is 0% for outbound royalties and interest paid by a SARL to non-residents, provided the payments are at arm's length and not recharacterized as hidden dividends or subject to anti-abuse rules; treaty rates therefore serve mainly as fallback protections against source-country or secondary recharacterization exposure.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 1,000,000 per related-party transaction category or in aggregate as specified by Luxembourg reporting practice; Form 1001 TP transfer-pricing disclosure is required with the annual CIT return when thresholds are met. Local File and Master File must be produced upon tax authority request; Country-by-Country Reporting applies at consolidated group revenue over EUR 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not maintain UAE-style ESR categories, but substance is enforced through GAAR, ATAD, tax ruling practice and the 2022 substance guidance. A SARL must demonstrate physical presence, employees, active management decisions and real economic risk in Luxembourg; letterbox structures or conduit arrangements will be recharacterized and denied treaty/domestic exemption benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately under-declaring rail freight revenues, using false intermodal transport invoices, or inflating related-party logistics costs to reduce Luxembourg taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment at the aggregate 24.94% rate, plus monthly late-payment interest of 0.6%; administrative penalties up to 20% of evaded tax; criminal tax fraud conviction can lead to significant fines and imprisonment up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false returns or direct tax evasion may be held jointly and severally liable for unpaid tax; civil restitution, travel bans, asset freezes and imprisonment can result from criminal conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure and Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file Form 1001 TP or failing to maintain arm's-length documentation for container leasing, haulage subcontracting, management fees and interest paid to foreign related parties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disallowance of deductions, recharacterization of transactions, tax reassessment at up to 24.94%, late-payment interest, and administrative penalties for incomplete or inaccurate transfer pricing disclosure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false or unsupported transfer-pricing statements can be personally liable for additional tax when the SARL is unable to pay; criminal sanctions apply in cases of intentional concealment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Artificial Arrangement and Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Luxembourg SARL as a letterbox company without personnel, premises, decision-making or commercial risk, solely to route rail freight payments and dividends through Luxembourg to obtain tax treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of GAAR/ATAD to disregard the entity or recharacterize payments as hidden dividends subject to 15% withholding tax; denial of DTA benefits, participation exemption and IP regime; possible net wealth tax and exit tax consequences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for unremitted withholding tax on recharacterized dividend distributions; continuing artificial arrangements can trigger criminal tax fraud exposure and travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using rail freight forwarding invoices, over- or under-invoicing intermodal logistics services, or shell supplier companies to launder proceeds or move value without economic rationale.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Breach of the Luxembourg AML/CFT law of 12 November 2004: administrative fines up to EUR 1,250,000; money laundering convictions carry imprisonment and confiscation of assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: AML compliance officers and directors can be personally fined or imprisoned; serious violations may result in removal from office, travel bans and personal restitution of illicitly transferred proceeds.
